rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L137 (maintainer 'Close shape') is the only maintainer text on the two module-owned forcing-function beats, L66-72 (prompt demands named omissions) and L74-80 (prompt forbids merging a disagreement): 'a team-lead move that lays three rules files side by side and records disagreement as open questions rather than merging it away'. It names a design intent, not (a) the dominant student failure (accepting the summary unread; folding three files into one agreed list) and not (b) an escape hatch (a recovery prompt or trainer move). The debrief key is borrowed from Agents 101 and the team-rules beat has no leaf file, so no other file carries them. Harm (a trainer with no lookup when the team merges its disagreement away or skips a rules file) is present; the rule says the story judge blocks ship without both.

resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §47 (Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch; the rule says the story judge blocks ship without both) line 137: harm: Grant that §47 applies literally: the maintainer block at L137 states the design intent and does not name a failure mode or an escape hatch. That is true. It still fails the harm lens.

(d) The meaning already ships in other lines. Debrief: the body names the dominant failure and its catch at L72. "Read its summary. Push back on anything that doesn't match the day... What Claude leaves out is often the signal. A tidy summary that skips the moment you re-prompted three times is the tell." The prompt `a101-m2-debrief-claude-md` also requires a grounding session moment for each rule and at least one named omission. The judge's proposed recovery, "ask Claude which summary line no session moment grounds", repeats what the prompt already demands. Team rules: the judge's failure mode, "folds three files into one list", is blocked by the prompt itself (`apt101-d1-team-rules`: "Don't merge a disagreement into a compromise"; disagreements go to a separate "Open questions for Day 2" part under each author's name). The body adds "Agree on nothing yet." Adding a trainer note for a failure the forcing function already prevents is tidiness.

Sibling precedent: the story judge on the sibling `learn-faster-than-the-market.md` gave §47 a PASS on a failure mode and catch carried in the body. The same reading clears this file. The canonical Agents 101 module (`agents-101/building-agent-systems.md`) is taught to real cohorts and uses the same debrief key with near-identical body text ("A clean summary that... skips the messy fourth... is the tell"). Its story instance has PASS and no §47 finding. So the judge's claim that "no other file carries them" is only literally true. The Agents 101 source carries the same failure and catch in its body, and the story judge accepted that there.

(c) The fix costs something. The proposed recovery, "ask which rule each of the other two would strike, and file the answer as an open question", invites the trio to start the strike-or-keep argument on Day 1. L80 deliberately defers it ("Agree on nothing yet"; the team file is read at Day 2 close per the artefact table at L133). The fix would cut into a deliberate beat.

(a)/(b) Nobody is worse off. The training is `simulation: true` (L103, site/layouts/curriculum.js:137): never taught, no trainer in a room, and the maintainer reads every page when the flag comes off. The claimed harm, "a trainer has no lookup", just restates the rule. The failures it describes are already caught by the body and the prompts.
